A Reuters investigation, based on internal documents and interviews, has revealed that the Chinese embassy in Manila paid a local marketing firm to wage a covert cyber campaign in the Philippines.

The operation was run by InfinitUs Marketing Solutions, a Manila-based, Chinese-owned company that was tasked with "guiding public opinion" on behalf of the embassy, according to a review of the firm's internal contracts and work-progress reports.

The primary tool of the campaign was a "troll army" of fake Facebook profiles created by InfinitUs to masquerade as pro-Beijing Filipino citizens, posting comments and sharing content to support China's agenda.

The campaign's objectives were to weaken domestic support for the Philippine government's maritime claims in the South China Sea and to sow discord over Manila's security alliance with the United States.

Internal reports show specific examples of the troll army's work, including propagating content about the "cons" of the U.S. deploying Typhon missiles in the Philippines.

Another key focus of the disinformation campaign was health. The fake accounts circulated negative articles about Western-made COVID-19 vaccines while simultaneously praising China's Sinovac shot.

The operation also involved targeted harassment. The fake accounts were used to "swarm" the social media pages of Filipino politicians critical of China, such as then-Congressman Robert Ace Barbers, flooding their posts with hundreds of negative comments and accusations.

To amplify its message, InfinitUs created a proxy media outlet called "Ni Hao Manila," which was designed to look like a legitimate Filipino-run news source but was used to post videos criticizing U.S.-Philippines security cooperation.

In a parallel effort to cultivate influence, the Chinese embassy funded cash awards which were distributed by the Association of Philippines-China Understanding (APCU), an organization with ties to the Chinese Communist Party.

These awards, worth thousands of dollars, were given to dozens of prominent Filipino officials, academics, and media personalities. A separate Philippine security agency report, seen by Reuters, had identified several of these same individuals as "instruments for Chinese influence."

This covert influence campaign has been unfolding as the Philippines, under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., strengthens its security ties with the United States—a sharp reversal from the pro-Beijing policy of his predecessor, Rodrigo Duterte.

A former senior Philippine official told Reuters that the "end goal" of China's campaign is to make the country "compliant" with Beijing's interests, and the report notes that polls show the pro-Beijing former president's daughter is a frontrunner for the 2028 presidential election.

data.raw_text:
ICYMI O/N

MACRO:

US President Trump opened the door to a possible end to the shutdown impasse by saying he’d negotiate with Democrats on health care subsidies, but later signaled he’d only talk once the government reopened. The Senate again rejected a stopgap bill. (BBG)

The White House on Monday backed off President Trump's assertion that government employees were already being laid off due to the shutdown, but warned job losses could result as the standoff looked set to stretch into a seventh day. (RTRS)

Goldman Sachs has raised its December 2026 gold price forecast to USD 4,900/oz vs prev. USD 4,300/oz. Said it sees risks to upgraded gold price forecast as still skewed to the upside. (Newsquawk)

Derivatives strategists at Societe Generale believe there is enough uncertainty to keep longer-term price swings elevated and recommend buying medium-term VIX futures and S&P forward volatility. The uptrend in volatility appears to be in place, they note. (BBG)

Fed's Schmid signaled he is disinclined to cut interest rates further, arguing that as the Fed navigates between the twin risks of overly tight and overly easy policy, it should stay focused on the danger of too-high inflation. (RTRS)

Japanese media have reported some within the Komeito party are considering pushing to leave the coalition citing worries over new LDP leader Sanae Takaichi's right-wing nature. Takaichi and the LDP's new leadership team are expected to meet with Komeito Tuesday, whose leader Tetsuo Saito voiced concerns over Takaichi's conservative views on Japan's wartime history and foreign residents. (BBG)

Japan’s 30yr sovereign bond auction demand was firm enough to calm a jittery market. The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.41, compared with 3.31 at the previous auction and a 12-month average of 3.37. Government bond futures pared losses after the result. (BBG)

The BoJ said its 2025 Paris Europlace Forum in Tokyo scheduled for Wednesday was called off and Governor Kazuo Ueda’s speech was canceled as a result. The BOJ made the announcement on the cancellation in a notice to reporters. (BBG)

Japan’s household spending rose for a fourth month, showing resilience amid persistent inflation. Outlays by households adjusted for inflation gained 2.3% from a year ago in August, led by spending on transport and entertainment. The result beat the median economist estimate of a 1.2% increase. (BBG) 

A large part of yen selling Monday was macro hedge funds closing bullish bets, or “squaring up,” rather than establishing new bearish ones, according to traders from Nomura International and Citigroup Inc. (BBG)

Japan is to expand its export controls on dual-use technologies from October 9th. Japan will expand export controls to cover general-purpose machine tools, integrated circuits, drones, radar, navigation, and testing equipment, requiring companies to verify potential military use. (DigiTimes)

Japan’s Finance Minister Kato said he will closely watch any excessive moves in the forex market, repeating that it is important for currencies to move stably while reflecting fundamentals. (BBG)

SMBC Nikko strategists upped their year-end prediction for Japan’s Nikkei 225 on expectations large-cap defense and tech stocks will outperform under Sanae Takaichi’s premiership. Raising Oct-Dec forecast range for Nikkei to 43,000-49,000 from 41,000-47,000, and end-Dec target to 47,000 from 45,000; maintains Topix outlook at 2,900-3,300 for Oct-Dec and 3,150 for end-Dec. (BBG)

The World Bank lifted its 2025 growth projection for China to 4.8% from 4.0% and 2026 to 4.2% from 4.0%, whilst raising its forecast for much of the Asia region, but warned of a slowing momentum next year, citing low consumer and business confidence and weak new export orders. (RTRS)

China's foreign exchange reserves increased more than expected last month, official data showed on Tuesday, as the dollar wobbled against other major currencies. (RTRS)

European value stocks are set to benefit from the current risk-on backdrop, as crowded momentum trades may falter into earnings season, according to Barclays strategists. The team led by Emmanuel Makonga upgrades value stocks to positive and downgrades low-volatility stocks to negative. (BBG)

German factory orders unexpectedly fell for a fourth month, another setback to the government as it struggles to lift Europe’s biggest economy out of two years of contraction. Demand declined 0.8% in August, with large orders preventing an even sharper drop. Economists polled by Bloomberg had predicted a 1.2% gain, with just one analyst anticipating a decrease. (BBG)

UK house prices fell from an all-time high in September, according to Halifx, suggesting fears of tax rises are dampening demand from prospective homebuyers. (BBG)

UK Chancellor Reeves is set to get help from inflation to finalize her plans for patching up the UK's budgetary black hole. Inflation is likely to deliver a net £5 billion boost to the chancellor's plans by lifting the taxable value of incomes, profits and prices in cash terms. The boost to tax revenue from higher prices and pay packets will more than offset the hit from lofty interest costs, resulting in a net boost to receipts, according to Michael Saunders' analysis. (BBG)

UK Chancellor Reeves does not have a credible plan to grow the economy and get debt down, according to Sir Charlie Bean, one of Britain’s most respected economists who has held senior posts at the OBR and BoE. (Telegraph)

Tech investors will quit Britain if Labour keep raising taxes, according to https://t.co/zD4SA017zd founder Brent Hoberman, who said venture capital (VC) funds were drawing up plans to move to Europe amid fears of a fresh raid in November. (Telegraph)

UK PM Starmer will lead a delegation of more than 100 British business, academic and cultural leaders to India, as he seeks to deepen commerce between the two countries after signing a long-awaited free trade agreement. (BBG)

Australian consumer confidence fell last week as the RBA left rates on hold and signaled that the inflation outlook might limit further cuts. Consumer confidence fell 1.2 points last week to 85.1 points, according to the ANZ Bank and pollster Roy Morgan. (WSJ)

Australian job advertisements fell sharply in September, an ANZ survey showed on Tuesday, in another sign the labour market was loosening as employment growth slows. (RTRS)

New Zealand businesses were less optimistic in the third quarter, raising the risk of another recession and deeper interest-rate cuts from the central bank. (BBG)

New Zealand's central bank said on Tuesday it would form a new financial policy committee that would give it the power to set prudential requirements for banks and help it to make decisions over mortgage lending ratios. (RTRS)

Vietnam is preparing for a decision on Tuesday by index provider FTSE Russell that could upgrade its stock market to emerging status alongside China and India, potentially unlocking billions of dollars in foreign investment. (RTRS)

Argentina’s government sold dollars in the foreign-exchange market Monday for a fifth straight session as it tries to stem a slide in the peso, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

Argentines are losing patience with Milei’s sluggish economy. (FT)

GEOPOLITICAL:

EU to curb Russian diplomats’ travel as suspected spy attacks mount. (FT)  

EQUITIES:

AMD has been upgraded by Jefferies to buy from hold with its price target raised to $300 from $170. Analyst Blayne Curtis says the OpenAI chip deal is a “strong validation” of AMD’s AI roadmap and the level of AI demand in general. “The partnership has the potential to generate well over $100B from OAI, new, and existing customers over the next four years”. (BBG)

Tesla plans to unveil a cheaper version of the Model Y on Tuesday, according to Bloomberg sources, following through on assurances it will have a more affordable vehicle to counter the loss of US incentives for electric vehicles. (BBG)

Elon Musk named a former Morgan Stanley executive the CFO of xAI, the Financial Times reported, appointing an ally to help oversee one of the largest US artificial intelligence startups. (FT)

Exxon Mobil said refining margins rebounded in the third quarter, adding about $500 million to earnings compared with the three months prior. (BBG)

A fire at Novelis’s Oswego, N.Y., plant, which supplies about 40% of U.S. auto industry aluminum, will disrupt automakers for months. Ford, the largest user of the plant’s aluminum for its F-150, may flag implications to investors, according to WSJ sources. (WSJ)

The International Energy Agency slashed in half its forecast of US renewable energy growth by 2030, even as the rest of the world races to double its green power capacity over the same period. (BBG)

Alibaba had its price target hiked to HK$220 from HK$172; for US-listed stock to $225 from $176. The analyst said the Chinese tech giant has repositioned itself as a “full-stack AI service provider.” (BBG)

Rheinmetall rival slams ‘direct award’ to German arms group. (FT)

Australia's corporate regulator approves Cboe Global Markets' application to operate as listing market in country, enabling it to compete directly with Australian Securities Exchange, other market operators. (RTRS)

data.english_translation: ICYMI O/N MACRO: US President Trump opened the door to a possible end to the shutdown impasse by saying he’d negotiate with Democrats on health care subsidies, but later signaled he’d only talk once the government reopened. The Senate again rejected a stopgap bill. (BBG) The White House on Monday backed off President Trump's assertion that government employees were already being laid off due to the shutdown, but warned job losses could result as the standoff looked set to stretch into a seventh day. (RTRS) Goldman Sachs has raised its December 2026 gold price forecast to USD 4,900/oz vs prev. USD 4,300/oz. Said it sees risks to upgraded gold price forecast as still skewed to the upside. (Newsquawk) Derivatives strategists at Societe Generale believe there is enough uncertainty to keep longer-term price swings elevated and recommend buying medium-term VIX futures and S&P forward volatility. The uptrend in volatility appears to be in place, they note. (BBG) Fed's Schmid signaled he is disinclined to cut interest rates further, arguing that as the Fed navigates between the twin risks of overly tight and overly easy policy, it should stay focused on the danger of too-high inflation. (RTRS) Japanese media have reported some within the Komeito party are considering pushing to leave the coalition citing worries over new LDP leader Sanae Takaichi's right-wing nature. Takaichi and the LDP's new leadership team are expected to meet with Komeito Tuesday, whose leader Tetsuo Saito voiced concerns over Takaichi's conservative views on Japan's wartime history and foreign residents. (BBG) Japan’s 30yr sovereign bond auction demand was firm enough to calm a jittery market. The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.41, compared with 3.31 at the previous auction and a 12-month average of 3.37. Government bond futures pared losses after the result. (BBG) The BoJ said its 2025 Paris Europlace Forum in Tokyo scheduled for Wednesday was called off and Governor Kazuo Ueda’s speech was canceled as a result. The BOJ made the announcement on the cancellation in a notice to reporters. (BBG) Japan’s household spending rose for a fourth month, showing resilience amid persistent inflation. Outlays by households adjusted for inflation gained 2.3% from a year ago in August, led by spending on transport and entertainment. The result beat the median economist estimate of a 1.2% increase. (BBG) A large part of yen selling Monday was macro hedge funds closing bullish bets, or “squaring up,” rather than establishing new bearish ones, according to traders from Nomura International and Citigroup Inc. (BBG) Japan is to expand its export controls on dual-use technologies from October 9th. Japan will expand export controls to cover general-purpose machine tools, integrated circuits, drones, radar, navigation, and testing equipment, requiring companies to verify potential military use. (DigiTimes) Japan’s Finance Minister Kato said he will closely watch any excessive moves in the forex market, repeating that it is important for currencies to move stably while reflecting fundamentals. (BBG) SMBC Nikko strategists upped their year-end prediction for Japan’s Nikkei 225 on expectations large-cap defense and tech stocks will outperform under Sanae Takaichi’s premiership. Raising Oct-Dec forecast range for Nikkei to 43,000-49,000 from 41,000-47,000, and end-Dec target to 47,000 from 45,000; maintains Topix outlook at 2,900-3,300 for Oct-Dec and 3,150 for end-Dec. (BBG) The World Bank lifted its 2025 growth projection for China to 4.8% from 4.0% and 2026 to 4.2% from 4.0%, whilst raising its forecast for much of the Asia region, but warned of a slowing momentum next year, citing low consumer and business confidence and weak new export orders. (RTRS) China's foreign exchange reserves increased more than expected last month, official data showed on Tuesday, as the dollar wobbled against other major currencies. (RTRS) European value stocks are set to benefit from the current risk-on backdrop, as crowded momentum trades may falter into earnings season, according to Barclays strategists. The team led by Emmanuel Makonga upgrades value stocks to positive and downgrades low-volatility stocks to negative. (BBG) German factory orders unexpectedly fell for a fourth month, another setback to the government as it struggles to lift Europe’s biggest economy out of two years of contraction. Demand declined 0.8% in August, with large orders preventing an even sharper drop. Economists polled by Bloomberg had predicted a 1.2% gain, with just one analyst anticipating a decrease. (BBG) UK house prices fell from an all-time high in September, according to Halifx, suggesting fears of tax rises are dampening demand from prospective homebuyers. (BBG) UK Chancellor Reeves is set to get help from inflation to finalize her plans for patching up the UK's budgetary black hole. Inflation is likely to deliver a net £5 billion boost to the chancellor's plans by lifting the taxable value of incomes, profits and prices in cash terms. The boost to tax revenue from higher prices and pay packets will more than offset the hit from lofty interest costs, resulting in a net boost to receipts, according to Michael Saunders' analysis. (BBG) UK Chancellor Reeves does not have a credible plan to grow the economy and get debt down, according to Sir Charlie Bean, one of Britain’s most respected economists who has held senior posts at the OBR and BoE. (Telegraph) Tech investors will quit Britain if Labour keep raising taxes, according to founder Brent Hoberman, who said venture capital (VC) funds were drawing up plans to move to Europe amid fears of a fresh raid in November. (Telegraph) UK PM Starmer will lead a delegation of more than 100 British business, academic and cultural leaders to India, as he seeks to deepen commerce between the two countries after signing a long-awaited free trade agreement. (BBG) Australian consumer confidence fell last week as the RBA left rates on hold and signaled that the inflation outlook might limit further cuts. Consumer confidence fell 1.2 points last week to 85.1 points, according to the ANZ Bank and pollster Roy Morgan. (WSJ) Australian job advertisements fell sharply in September, an ANZ survey showed on Tuesday, in another sign the labour market was loosening as employment growth slows. (RTRS) New Zealand businesses were less optimistic in the third quarter, raising the risk of another recession and deeper interest-rate cuts from the central bank. (BBG) New Zealand's central bank said on Tuesday it would form a new financial policy committee that would give it the power to set prudential requirements for banks and help it to make decisions over mortgage lending ratios. (RTRS) Vietnam is preparing for a decision on Tuesday by index provider FTSE Russell that could upgrade its stock market to emerging status alongside China and India, potentially unlocking billions of dollars in foreign investment. (RTRS) Argentina’s government sold dollars in the foreign-exchange market Monday for a fifth straight session as it tries to stem a slide in the peso, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG) Argentines are losing patience with Milei’s sluggish economy. (FT) GEOPOLITICAL: EU to curb Russian diplomats’ travel as suspected spy attacks mount. (FT) EQUITIES: AMD has been upgraded by Jefferies to buy from hold with its price target raised to $300 from $170. Analyst Blayne Curtis says the OpenAI chip deal is a “strong validation” of AMD’s AI roadmap and the level of AI demand in general. “The partnership has the potential to generate well over $100B from OAI, new, and existing customers over the next four years”. (BBG) Tesla plans to unveil a cheaper version of the Model Y on Tuesday, according to Bloomberg sources, following through on assurances it will have a more affordable vehicle to counter the loss of US incentives for electric vehicles. (BBG) Elon Musk named a former Morgan Stanley executive the CFO of xAI, the Financial Times reported, appointing an ally to help oversee one of the largest US artificial intelligence startups. (FT) Exxon Mobil said refining margins rebounded in the third quarter, adding about $500 million to earnings compared with the three months prior. (BBG) A fire at Novelis’s Oswego, N.Y., plant, which supplies about 40% of U.S. auto industry aluminum, will disrupt automakers for months. Ford, the largest user of the plant’s aluminum for its F-150, may flag implications to investors, according to WSJ sources. (WSJ) The International Energy Agency slashed in half its forecast of US renewable energy growth by 2030, even as the rest of the world races to double its green power capacity over the same period. (BBG) Alibaba had its price target hiked to HK$220 from HK$172; for US-listed stock to $225 from $176. The analyst said the Chinese tech giant has repositioned itself as a “full-stack AI service provider.” (BBG) Rheinmetall rival slams ‘direct award’ to German arms group. (FT) Australia's corporate regulator approves Cboe Global Markets' application to operate as listing market in country, enabling it to compete directly with Australian Securities Exchange, other market operators.
